mission.title: Did We Need to Do That?

theory.title: Needn't have done frente a didn't need to
theory.explanation: Usa needn't have + participio cuando alguien hizo algo que no era necesario. Usa didn't need to cuando no había necesidad, pero no siempre indica si la acción llegó a realizarse. I needn't have booked significa que reservé, pero no hacía falta; I didn't need to book indica que no era necesario reservar.
theory.tip: Needn't have done: lo hiciste, pero no hacía falta. Didn't need to: no era necesario; no confirma si lo hiciste.

grammar.english: I needn't have bought bottled water; there was a fountain.
grammar.spanish: Needn't have done vs didn't need to: ejemplo 1
grammar.note: Use needn't have + past participle when someone did something that was unnecessary. Use didn't need to when there was no necessity; it does not always say whether the action happened. Compare: I needn't have booked (I booked, but it was unnecessary); I didn't need to book (there was no need).

content.passage: On Saturday, Laura went to a fitness class for the first time. She arrived thirty minutes early, but she needn't have hurried because the instructor was late. She had brought a towel, although she didn't need to because the centre provided one. She also bought a bottle of water, but she needn't have done that because there was a drinking fountain. Next time, she knows she won't need to prepare so much.

items.prompt: Describe something you did that was unnecessary.

When I feel stressed, I take a break or go for a walk. It is important to follow medical advice and ask questions when something is unclear. Small changes can make a big difference over time, especially when people keep practising them.

content.audioTranscript: A: Have you got your appointment tomorrow? B: Yes, I want to talk about my daily routine. A: Are you doing enough exercise? B: I'm trying to. The doctor gave me some useful advice. A: What did they suggest? B: Drinking more water and getting enough sleep. A: Do you need any medicine? B: No, but I need to rest during my recovery. A: I hope you feel better by tomorrow.
